entries.title: Victoria of Many Faces
entries.jpTitle: 手札が多めのビクトリア

review.en:
Episode #7: I Made Great Memories

What even was that… an absolute gem.

There was clearly far more going on beneath the surface in the subtle exchanges between the baron and his wife, the aunt, and in the atmosphere between Nonna and Victoria than what was explicitly shown. And what made it even better was that the episode only showed what could actually be seen and inferred, rather than forcing extra drama through overt direction or exaggerated presentation.

The exchange with the retired soldier who arranged the horse, the way he saw through Victoria's true identity and how that shaped what she decided to do next, her relationship with the captain, the dynamic between the woman she met through the pickpocket and her maid, the captain's older brother… There was so much depth everywhere.

Even the sequence explaining why Nonna decided to stay for six days in the first place was handled really well.

If I had to nitpick one thing, it would be: how exactly did Nonna, after sneaking out, manage to come back? And did her return really need to be staged in such an ominous, suspicious-looking way? Then again, you could also read that as showing just how completely Victoria failed to imagine that Nonna might actually come home that way, so maybe even that choice had a point.

Forget just another two episodes—please give this another two cours.
review.jp:
第7話: 素敵な思い出ができたのは

『なんだコレ・・・珠玉。男爵夫妻とおばさんの微妙なやり取りとノンナとビクトリアの間の空気も、全然そこからみてとれた以上のものがあったが、見て取れる部分だけをちゃんと見せていて、それ以上にドラマチックにしたいからという演出上の見せ方ではなかったのも素晴らしかった。馬を手配してくれた退役軍人とのやり取り、正体を見透かしそれ故に今後の行動も決める流れ、また隊長とのあり方、スリを介して知り合ったおばさんとお手伝いさんの感じ、隊長のアニキ・・・、なんと深い・・・。またそもそも何故ノンナが即6日間滞在することにしたかの流れも良かった。唯一ちょっとだけ言うなら、抜け出してきたノンナはどうやって帰ってきた?またあんなに思わせぶりに不審者っぽくしなくていいんじゃない?というのもあったが、それくらいヴィクトリアはノンナの帰宅を想像していなかったともとれるので、意味はあったのかも知れない。あと2話と言わず、もう2クールくらい放送してください。』

entries.synopsis: In an age when spies act behind the scenes in every land, Chloe spends her days successfully carrying out even the most difficult missions due to her unparalleled disguise skills and martial arts abilities. After the betrayal of her boss, she suddenly disappears—as Chloe plans to redo her life as the ordinary citizen Victoria in the neighboring kingdom of Ashberry, striving for a “normal” life. However, Victoria's peaceful life is abruptly cut short as she begins to get involved with many people. In this new land, her experiences and abilities from her days as a spy come in far more useful than she ever expected! On the other hand, the second prince--and others--take an interest in Victoria's strength, and the shadows close in on the woman with many faces…  (Source: Yen Press)

entries.title: Draw This, Then Die!

review.en:
Episode #8: Tatchi: Manga de Egakitai Hyaku no Koto!!!

That was excellent. This episode focused almost entirely on the teacher’s past, and I really liked seeing how her time working as an assistant gradually connected to the creation of Robota and Pokota. It was also great to finally see how that earlier moment at Comitia, when her work was described as having “murderous intent,” fit into the bigger picture.

Her meeting with the used-bookstore owner from Oshima, and the way that relationship connects to everything we have seen up to now, was also really well done. The structure was excellent too, with the students appearing before and after the flashback and neatly framing the entire episode.
review.jp:
第8話: タッチ〜漫画で描きたい100のコト!!

『いや、素晴らしかった。今回はほぼ先生の過去だが、彼女がアシをやりながら如何にロボタとポコ太につながっていくのか、また以前にコミュティアで「殺意」と言われたのかが繋がっていたのも良かった。また大島出身の古本屋の人との出会いと今までの繋がりもいいい。その前後に生徒たちが描かれていた構成も申し分なかった。』

entries.synopsis: First-year high school student Ai Yasumi lives on the island of Izu Oshima and loves reading manga. But after a certain turning point, she sets her sights on creating stories of her own! As she dives into the world of manga-making, Ai faces challenges, growth, and the excitement of chasing her creative dreams. Where will her creative journey take her?  (Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: The World Is Dancing
entries.jpTitle: ワールド イズ ダンシング

review.en:
Episode #8: To the Other Side of the Bridge

I think this was the best episode so far. That said, I do think the final part, where Oniyasha and Zojiro end up performing together, could have been handled differently—something less tacked-on and poppy would have worked better.

The same goes for the way Oniyasha’s overwhelming talent is presented mostly through words and established assumptions rather than being fully shown. And with the other character as well, instead of revealing his entire past all at once through a flashback, I wish there had been more gradual buildup. If the series had also spent more time earlier on properly developing Dengaku itself and the relationships among the performers, I think this episode could have scored even higher, which is a shame.

Still, it does feel like things could get more interesting from here. We’ll see.
review.jp:
第8話: 橋の向こうへ

『今までで一番良かったと思う。鬼夜叉と増次郎の2人が一緒にやることになる最後の部分はもうちょっと違った描き方、あんなとって付けのポップなのじゃないものであっても良かったと思うし、鬼夜叉の圧倒的な才能を言葉や前提として見せるのではなく・・・ってのももだけど、もう一人の方も回想で一気に過去を見せるのではなくもうちょっと積み重ねがあったり、田楽のこれまでや仲間との関係ももうすこし今までにしっかり描けていればもっと高い点が採れたと思うので残念。今後は面白くなりそうでもあるがどうだろうか・・・。』

entries.synopsis: Born into a life of acting and dance with a traveling theater troupe in 14th-century Japan, 12-year old Oniyasha has one problem—he doesn't know what the point of any of it is. "Why must I step with the left foot here instead of the right? Why is one performance good and another, bad? Why do people dance at all?" It all seems perfectly arbitrary, until a chance encounter in a run-down shack sets him down a path to revolutionizing the art form and influencing much of Japanese culture to come. A fictionalized account of the early life of Zeami Motokiyo (Oniyasha), the founder of modern Noh theater—the world's oldest surviving theater art—this coming-of-age artist's journey vividly brings to life a man far ahead of his time during one of Japan's most culturally and socially vibrant eras.  (Source: Kodansha Comics)

entries.title: From Old Country Bumpkin to Master Swordsman Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 片田舎のおっさん、剣聖になるII

review.en:
Episode #7: The Old Country Bumpkin Gets an Invitation from Nobility

The extra material went a little too far, but I thought everything up through Beryl visiting his former noble student was excellent.

The production quality was high, of course, but what really worked for me was the subtle, delicate way the episode handled Mewi at the dorm, as well as the young man at the tavern who asked Beryl for guidance and the woman he cared about. Beryl's advice—something along the lines of, "Wouldn't it be enough for the two of you to grow together?"—also felt meaningful because of what had happened with his father, and you could really sense Beryl's own growth through it. For a while, it felt like all of the series' strengths suddenly came together at once.

But then the latter part hit me with a serious "not this again…" feeling and really killed my enthusiasm. The teacher suddenly becoming irresistible to everyone, and then getting aggressively pursued by the younger sister of his former noble student… it just sounds painfully uninteresting.

Still, the first half was strong enough that I'm giving it a 9.
review.jp:
第7話: 片田舎のおっさん、貴族に招かれる

『ちょっとオマケが過ぎるが貴族のもと教え子を尋ねるまでは凄く良かったと思う。クオリティも高いが、寮や酒場でのミュイや指南を願い出た青年とその想い人の描き方微妙で繊細な描き方、ベリルの共に成長をするというのではダメなのかな?といった助言にも父親との件があったゆえの彼の成長が感じられたり、本作の魅力が一気に出た?と感じられる良いものだった。だが、その後が、"またこの展開かよ・・・"といったものでかなり萎えた。先生がモテモテになる、、、元教え子貴族の妹に迫られる・・・つまんなそう・・・。でも前半が良かったので9点。』

entries.romanized_title: Saijo no Osewa: Takane no Hanadarake na Meimonkou de, Gakuin Ichi no Ojou-sama (Seikatsu Nouryoku Kaimu) wo Kagenagara Osewa suru Koto ni Narimashita
entries.synopsis: Hinako Konohana is the perfect young lady—graceful, elegant, and flawless… or so everyone thinks. Behind closed doors, she’s a total disaster who can’t handle basic chores! When ordinary student Itsuki Tomonari becomes her caretaker, he’s thrown into 24/7 damage control, maintaining her “perfect” image. It’s awkward, nonstop chaos—but it starts softening into something that feels like love…  (Source: Crunchyroll)

review.jp:
第7話: 特別、だから

『何というか・・・なんとも言えないチグハグな構成と脚本。それぞれのパートを見るとそこまで悪くない感じもあるのに全体として噛み合わない不自然さモリモリ。２人の女子とお手々繋ぐのは良くわからない対比?親父のセリフも不躾に放り込みまくりの不自然さ。今回初めての登場なのに何だか・・・。演出力がなさすぎ。意味あるのか無いのかも良くわからないカットも多いし。』

entries.romanized_title: Tenkousaki no Seiso Karen na Bishoujo ga, Mukashi Danshi to Omotte Issho ni Asonda Osananajimi datta Ken
entries.synopsis: Seven years after making a childhood promise to always be friends, Hayato is reunited with his formerly tomboyish pal Haruki at a city high school–only now, Haruki has transformed into the girl every guy dreams about! While Haruki’s looks may have changed, with Hayato, she’s still the same pal he remembers. Despite years apart, their promise and feelings remain and deepen into something stronger.  (Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Love Unseen Beneath the Clear Night Sky
entries.jpTitle: 透明な夜に駆ける君と、目に見えない恋をした。

review.jp:
第7話: 透明

『何すかこれ?前回から構成も変だしおかしいよコレ。衝撃的に見せるための不自然な演出に違和感しか無い。唐突に見かけたと走ってくる友人。謎に走って病院に行く２人。何故タクシーに乗らない?走る?ガンが網膜に転移していた?その話は以前にしたんだよね?デートのときに。それを今初めて明かすの?それは反則でしかない。告白したら突然好き過ぎる感じになるし・・・。ダメだ・・・。』

entries.romanized_title: Toumei na Yoru ni Kakeru Kimi to, Me ni Mienai Koi wo Shita.
entries.synopsis: On an April night in Tokyo, still too early for fireworks, university student Kakeru Sorano meets a woman named Koharu Fuyutsuki. She is a beautiful girl who stands out from the crowd, laughs a lot, and exudes a warmth that contrasts sharply with Kakeru's own introversion. But there was something Kakeru didn't know at first—she can't see.  Unlike Kakeru, Koharu hasn't given up on anything, even with her blindness. She attends university daily, shows interest in clubs, makes friends—and dreams of launching fireworks one day. Kakeru wonders why, when she can't see them...but maybe it doesn't matter. And maybe he can start moving forward, too, for the girl who's always been by his side  (Source: Yen Press)
